Python data types are fundamental to the language, enabling you to represent various kinds of data. You use basic data types like int, float, and complex for numbers, str for text, bytes and bytearray for binary data, and bool for Boolean values. stories.title: 11 Beginner Tips for Learning Python Programming
stories.excerpt: Python tips for beginners: the learning strategies and habits that take you from your first script to code you're proud of.
stories.lead:
We are so excited that you have decided to embark on the journey of learning Python! One of the most common questions we receive from our readers is “What’s the best way to learn Python?”

I believe that the first step in learning any programming language is making sure that you understand how to learn. Learning how to learn is arguably the most critical skill involved in computer programming.

Why is knowing how to learn so important? The answer is simple: as languages evolve, libraries are created, and tools are upgraded. Knowing how to learn will be essential to keeping up with these changes and becoming a successful programmer.

stories.title: Australia investigating Flydubai co-pilot's links to country
stories.excerpt: State police and the country's security agency are looking into the co-pilot, who attempted to take control of a Flydubai plane travelling to Israel.
stories.lead:
Australian authorities are investigating the links between the country and a Flydubai co-pilot who attempted to take control of a plane travelling to Israel.

The co-pilot is alleged to have attacked the captain with a crash axe during a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv before passengers managed to overpower him and successfully take control of the plane.

The Australian authorities have not identified the co-pilot, who has been named by multiple media outlets including Reuters, CNN and The New York Times as Hamam al-Hammami.

stories.title: Crimson Fall in NWPC Opener
stories.excerpt: Men's water polo back in action Sunday at LIU, Iona.
stories.lead:
PRINCETON, N.J. -- The Harvard men's water polo team lost its conference opener to Princeton, 15-8, on the road Saturday afternoon. The loss dropped the Crimson 3-10 overall and 0-1 in the NWPC, while the No. 9 Tigers improved to 12-1 and 1-0.

It took several possessions for either offense to get into a rhythm and it was Princeton that struck first. Harvard pulled even at 2-2 on junior Dean Strauser's first goal of the game; a 5-meter penalty shot. Strauser, who led the Crimson in scoring, scored all three of his goals in the first half. His second and third goals of the game each came from distance with the third tying the game, 5-5.

stories.title: I clawed my way to the top but need a break - Azpilicueta
stories.excerpt: Cesar Azpilicueta says it is time to move to "a different stage of life" following a glorious 20-year playing career, notably captaining Chelsea to several titles.
stories.lead:
Cesar Azpilicueta was an all-encompassing leader for Chelsea - and, now retired, he reflects on how his passion for education and attention to detail helped him build a career at the highest level.

One story sums it up. Before Chelsea's Champions League final victory in 2021, Azpilicueta could not take his customary pre-match nap and opted to study instead.

He says his work towards an MBA in business management from the Berlin School of Business and Innovation took his mind off the pressure and noise on the streets of Porto.
